prompt: Which aspect of distribution does Lara want to read about?
evidence: Lara says she wants to read about the effects of managing all distribution from just one office, while noting that she already covered stock control in a previous paper.
why: Managing distribution from one office is centralisation, so option C matches her stated research interest.
trap: A: Lara explicitly says she studied stock control in last term's paper and would rather not revisit it. B: Delivery timing is mentioned as an issue in distribution, but it is not the specific topic she says she wants to research.
explanation: Lara wants to investigate the effects of centralising distribution management in a single office.

prompt: Lara believes that some multinational companies can be criticised for
evidence: Lara says multinationals often bring in their own management team, ride roughshod over everyone and fail to consult at local level.
why: Her criticism is specifically about replacing or bypassing local management with the multinational's own team.
trap: A: Lara says introducing new machinery can be acceptable or beneficial. B: She also says improved working conditions can be a positive result rather than the criticism she is making here.
explanation: Lara objects to companies imposing their own management teams without adequate local consultation.

prompt: The tutor gives the example of the supermarket chain to show how companies

options.text: can use new advertising methods to bring new business.
need time to build up their reputation.
may fail to take local values into consideration.

evidence: The supermarket handed out free plastic bags in a market that was strongly environmentally conscious, so the promotion clashed with local attitudes toward plastic waste.
why: The example demonstrates that a marketing strategy can fail when a company ignores local environmental values.
trap: A: The story is not mainly about a new advertising technique succeeding. B: Reputation-building time is not the lesson drawn from the example.
explanation: The supermarket's promotion was a mistake because it ignored the local market's environmental values.

prompt: Which aim of global marketing has Lara explained very clearly?
evidence: The tutor says Lara explained really well how companies going global are usually seeking a huge increase in sales. The production link needs clarification, and profits are suggested as a later point.
why: The tutor explicitly praises Lara's explanation of the increase in sales, which corresponds to maximising sales.
trap: A: The tutor says the link involving production in another country is not yet clear enough. C: Profit is something the tutor suggests Lara can link in afterwards to finish the section.
explanation: The clearest part of Lara's section is her explanation that global expansion aims to generate a major increase in sales.

prompt: Why has the manager arrived late at this meeting?

options.text: He had to take a guest to hospital.
He had to speak to head office.
He had to complete a report.

evidence: The assistant manager took the ill guest to hospital, while the manager was delayed because an urgent report had to be completed.
why: The manager's own delay was caused by having to finish the report, so option C is correct.
trap: A: The assistant manager, not the manager, took the guest to hospital. B: Speaking to head office is not given as the reason for the delay.
explanation: The manager arrived late because he had to finish an urgent report before attending the meeting.
